content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question regarding the PT100 sensor. The [company_name] factory designed an analog input in the [product_name] with article number [article_no]. How should I connect a PT100 to this [product_name]? Also, why did the factory include this analog input? In what situations is it used? Thank you for your support. Best regards, [user_name]

You cannot connect a PT100 sensor directly to the 0-10V analog input of the base module. You need to use an external converter with a 0-10V output, or a converter with a 0/4-20mA output (in which case you will also need a 500-ohm resistor) or an expansion module like [product_name] AM2 RTD.

That's correct. Where can the analog input included in this [product_name] with article number [article_no] be used? As far as I know, the [company_name] factory included 4 analog inputs. I only need to read and use the input in my process, without any analog output.

Are you posting in different forums to get answers for your question? In this forum, you received advice to use a PT100 sensor, for example, with an AM2 RTD module. This is not an output module, but an extension module with 2 inputs for PT100 or PT1000 sensors. If you want to use the analog inputs of the base module (which only accept 0-10V signals), try searching for a sensor with direct 0-10V output and the appropriate temperature range for your needs. The correct sensor depends on your application and what is available from suppliers where you live. There isn't a universal temperature sensor that works for every application. Regards, [user_name]

Hello, I need to read temperature from three locations, each around 3 to 4 meters away from the CPU. I know that longer wiring can affect sensor reliability. I didn't want to use PT100 or similar sensors because that requires an extension module. I would like to use the analog input that's already on the base module. I considered sensors with built-in ADCs, so I could connect them and use them in my program. Do you know of any sensors that fit this description, or can you suggest a part number or datasheet so I can order one from the manufacturer?

I recall reading this in another forum; it looks like you've copied it here. Have you read my previous response? I don't think so, otherwise you would have shared more details such as the application, the required temperature range, and the desired resolution. Regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], Your information about RTD sensors isn't entirely accurate. Why do you say the cable length limit for a PT100 is around 3 meters? Check the screenshot below from another manufacturer (Schneider) for reference. You could increase the distance from the controller by selecting an RTD (PT100 sensor) that includes a built-in transmitter (0-10V or 4-20mA output). Hope this helps, [user_name]

I've read your question, but I was hoping for more information about sensors with a 0-10V output. I thought that the [product_name] could read ADC values like a microprocessor with different ADC ranges, but as you explained, it only supports sensors with a voltage output. Thank you for the clarification.

Hello [user_name], [company_name] mentions in the manual for the [product_name] expansion module AM2 RTD that the maximum cable length between PT and module is 10 meters. I already explained in this topic that a PT sensor cannot be connected directly to a 0-10V analog input on the base module. If you want to use the 0-10V input, you need a converter with a 0-10V or 0/4-20mA output. I'm not sure why you are asking again.

I don't want to use an extension module, just the local input on the base module. I don't want to use additional modules. If I'm mistaken, please clarify whether this is possible with the module you recommended. Anyway, thank you for your advice.

You can order a PT100 sensor already fitted with a converter, offering either a 0-10V or 0/4-20mA output, or you can order the PT sensor and converter separately. For a 0/4-20mA output, you will also need a 500-ohm resistor to convert the current signal into a voltage signal for a 0-10V analog input. I can't provide exact part numbers or datasheets because I don't know your country, so links to German companies wouldn't help.

That's the issue—there aren't enough details, and we need to know you mean sensors with voltage output. You can't connect just any sensor to the [product_name] using serial protocols such as 1-Wire, I²C, or SPI. Check the operating instructions to see which signals are supported; there are no alternative methods. To find a suitable sensor, just use your preferred search engine. Regards, [user_name]

Simply buy a sensor for your required temperature range, for example 0-100°C or 0-200°C, along with a compatible PT100 transmitter. Multiple output types are available, such as 0-5V, 0-10V, 4-20mA, or Modbus RS485. For your application, I recommend a PT100 plus transmitter (4-20mA), combined with a 4-20mA-to-voltage converter. These units are adjustable or calibratable for accuracy.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are unsure how to connect PT100 temperature sensors to the analog inputs of the [product_name] base module, particularly regarding direct connections and the need for extra modules or converters. The main challenge is that PT100 sensors cannot be interfaced directly with the module's standard analog inputs (0-10V), so only sensors with matching output signals or the use of appropriate extension modules are possible. There is also confusion about wiring distances and the impact on measurement reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to connect PT100 sensors directly to the analog inputs on the [product_name] base module, without requiring extra converters or extension modules. Reliable temperature readings from sensors located several meters away using only the built-in analog inputs are desired.
